note: The one place the local engine's pins live: which llama.cpp build to fetch for each PC, and which models. Every fact was read from the live page named in its source, at the time given (IST). Nothing here is guessed: a platform or model that could not be confirmed is left out and listed under leftOut.

engine.name: llama.cpp
engine.licenceSource: LICENSE in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp at commit 46eb1742 (master), read 21 Nov 2026 12:03 IST: 'MIT License, Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors'
engine.releaseSource: git tags of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp read 21 Nov 2026 12:02 IST: b12603 was the newest tag but its files answered HTTP 404 (still building); b12602 was the newest release whose files download. The GitHub release API and release page were not reachable from this session (refused), so the file names come from the release workflow .github/workflows/release-publish.yml at commit 46eb1742 and each one was confirmed by downloading it.
engine.checksumSource: llama.cpp publishes no checksum file in its releases (release-publish.yml attaches only the archives and a build attestation). The SHA-256 of each file below was computed from the file downloaded from its release address on 21 Nov 2026 at 12:03:57 IST.
engine.serverSource: tools/server/README.md at commit 46eb1742 and 'llama-server --help' of build 12602 (Linux x64), read 21 Nov 2026 12:05 IST: --model, --host, --port, --ctx-size, --api-key-file, --no-webui, --offline, --jinja, --alias, --parallel, --reasoning exist; GET /health is public and answers 503 while the model loads and 200 when ready; POST /v1/chat/completions is OpenAI-compatible with streaming; OpenAI-style tool calls are supported with --jinja.
leftOut: Linux x64 with Vulkan (llama-b12602-bin-ubuntu-vulkan-x64.tar.gz exists): it needs the Vulkan loader installed on the PC, which the hardware scan cannot confirm, so Linux always gets the processor build.
CUDA builds for Windows and Linux: each needs a second archive with the CUDA libraries and a matching NVIDIA driver; not pinned. A PC with an NVIDIA card on Windows gets the Vulkan build instead.
ROCm, SYCL, OpenVINO, OpenCL Adreno and s390x builds: not pinned.

models.source: Hugging Face model API (https://huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>?expand[]=cardData&expand[]=gguf) and file list (https://huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>/tree/main), read 21 Nov 2026 12:06 IST. size and sha256 are the file's size and LFS object id as Hugging Face lists them; a download of the 1B file from its pinned commit answered x-linked-etag equal to that id. Licence from each model card's licence field (apache-2.0), confirmed in its README front matter. Tool calls: the GGUF's own chat template has a <tool_call> section.

list.name: Granite 4.0 1B
list.why: light, for PCs with little free memory

list.name: Granite 4.2 8B
list.why: stronger answers; needs a strong PC

models.needsGbNote: needsGb is an estimate made here: the file's size plus the context memory at 8192 tokens, rounded up. It is not a figure from the publisher.
